chunks: Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Tamim al-Sarkhasi, the jurist of Sarkhas, said: Abu Labib Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shami said: Harun ibn Abd Allah al-Jammal narrated to me from Abu Ayyub, who said: Qudamah ibn Muhraz al-Ashja'i narrated to me that Makhramah ibn Bakr ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Ashajj, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Harb ibn Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, said: I bear witness on my father, Zayd ibn Khalid, that I heard him say:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) sent me saying, 'Give glad tidings to the people that whoever says: There is no god but Allah, Alone, who has no partner, will have Paradise.'

key_terms.بَشِّرِ النَّاسَ: Give glad tidings to the people
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god but Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for entering Paradise according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *al-Tawhid*, this hadith emphasizes the sufficiency of sincere monotheism (*Tawhid*) as the ultimate criterion for Paradise, reflecting the Shia focus on the purity of creed (*Aqidah*) free from *Shirk*. The chain of narration highlights the transmission of this core message through the Prophet’s companions, underscoring its centrality in Islamic theology. This promise serves as both a spiritual incentive and a theological foundation for the belief that correct belief in God's oneness is the gateway to eternal salvation.
